raw_response:
I will keep my full 6.0 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my land and well irrigation, and at my age I want a simple, familiar plan with stable grain production rather than trying anything risky. I farm alone, so I will avoid management that is too labor-heavy, but I will still use better seed and enough fertilizer to protect yield. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, give moderate nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate about three times if water is available, and do rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing every season. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well to it, apply a bit more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate about two times depending on rain, and keep pesticide use limited but not zero. My goal is steady output from the 6 mu, not maximum yield, so I will manage inputs at a moderate level that I can afford and handle by myself.
